SADR contest_start with morocco, Feb 1976, 'W. Sahara' (331 cells, the Free Zone). The berm page: Polisario 'controls the mostly uninhabited "Free Zone", which comprises all areas to the east of the barrier'; the start (SADR proclamation, 27 Feb 1976) and the end (ceasefire 6 September 1991, closed by ledger/8) are quoted from the War page, which I opened too. Trial: the 156 Free Zone cells north of the Tiris are the republic's land contested by Morocco at end 1976-1990 and direct at end 1991; it merges into the pair's contest of ledger/3, so ledger/8 closes it.

Morocco occupation_start of SADR land, April 1976, Oued el Dahab minus Tiris al-Gharbiyya (47 cells, 24.0-24.54 N). The Western Sahara page: 'partitioned between Morocco and Mauritania in April 1976', Morocco 'acquiring the northern two-thirds'. The Tiris page (opened by me) gives Western Tiris 88,000 km2 while the gazetteer's Tiris (south of 24 N) already resolves to 401 cells, about 101,400 km2, so the 47 cells belong on the Moroccan side, not the Mauritanian. Trial: occupied by Morocco from end 1976 on; the published 2020 anchor had them direct republic.

Mauritania gain from the SADR, April 1976, Tiris al-Gharbiyya (401 cells). The Western Sahara page: partition 'in April 1976', 'Mauritania taking control of the southern third as Tiris al-Gharbiyya'; the Tiris page: 'Partition of Spanish Sahara: 14 April 1976'. It carries out mauritania/ledger/2 and the mauritania_1976 keyframe, which had moved nothing (snap 'kept by others' 195 -> 20 in my trial too). Trial: end 1976-1978 all 401 Tiris cells Mauritanian, contested by the republic; nothing Mauritanian is left in the territory after 1979. The region is the gazetteer's Tiris, 15% larger than the page's 88,000 km2 (a gazetteer matter, see problems).

Mauritania contest_start with the SADR, April 1976, Tiris al-Gharbiyya. The War page: Mauritania 'took control of the southern third', the war with Mauritania (Tichla and La Guera taken 20 December 1975) and 'A comprehensive peace treaty was signed on 5 August 1979'. Trial: the 401 Tiris cells striped Mauritania/republic at end 1976-1978 and no Mauritania-SADR contest left at end 1979 (closed by the land change and SADR ledger/5). It also gave Mauritania two coastal Tiris cells that were nobody's since 1970; harmless, they are the republic's from 1979.

SADR gain of the Tiris from morocco, August 1979. The War page: peace treaty '5 August 1979', Tiris al-Gharbiya 'unilaterally annexed by Morocco on 11 August 1979'; the Western Sahara page: Mauritania 'abandoned all claims to its portion in August 1979'. Undoes the effect of mauritania/ledger/3 (the Tiris handed to Morocco as Moroccan land, which made SADR ledger/7 read as the republic occupying Moroccan land). Trial: end 1979 the 401 Tiris cells are the republic's (226 occupied by Morocco, 175 contested); end 2019 the published reversal of Dakhla is gone.

SADR occupation_start by morocco, August 1979, Tiris minus 'W. Sahara' (226 cells, the Tiris west of the berm with Dakhla). The berm page gives the land ('the Polisario-controlled areas ... on the east', Dakhla inside the fifth wall); the August 1979 date is quoted in the note from the War page ('unilaterally annexed by Morocco on 11 August 1979'), and the Western Sahara page has 'Morocco moved to occupy that sector shortly thereafter' and 'Morocco occupies territory to the west of the berm'. Trial: 226 cells republic land occupied by Morocco from end 1979 to the 2020s.

SADR contest_start with morocco, August 1979, Tiris inside 'W. Sahara' (175 cells east of the berm). Morocco annexed the whole Tiris on 11 August 1979 (War page) but the land east of the barrier is the Polisario's Free Zone (berm page; Western Sahara page 'Approximately 30% ... controlled by the Polisario Front').
